title: Audit R437 bad-class proof against literal pivot routines
body:
PR #4176's fallback allowance depends on a low-field pivot decision remaining valid for every high lift and diagonal unit ancestry. This adds an independent, source-pinned audit in `research/r437-bad-class-pivot-audit/`. **No gap was found in that scoped implication under its explicit split-projector, fixed-chart, complete-cover and unit-weight premises.** The probability bound and construction remain credited to their predecessors; no new κ is claimed.

The written argument connects complementary minors to all intermediate pivot units, proves the full-ring Schur block vanishes for the declared split rank, and explains the literal `good_form` column reversal. Its reference checker uses separately written determinant/adjugate arithmetic and compares the original source routines, including actual binary Word/Ring execution.

Evidence:
- 25,008 exhaustive field/rank cases across GL2(F3/F5/F7) and GL3(F3), checking the signed complementary-minor identity, pivot ratios and all diagonal unit weights.
- All 3,888 GL2 lifts modulo 9 and 139,968 lift/diagonal-unit combinations.
- 61 fixtures through **both** literal binary pivot routines, plus 20 synthetic 64-dimensional source classifications at ranks 1,2,7,14,42.
- Explicit premise controls: nonzero nonunit pivot, a good final minor with a failed earlier pivot, false split rank, omitted determinant signs, incomplete low cover, nondiagonal weights, wrong high-digit multiplier and singular preparation.

Validation at `cc304c09c48103c20e7c0e2634b22d0aa19aa38a`: registered ordinary and optimized replays passed; metadata/source pins and committed-byte preflight passed for 14 files. The official export and integrity check passed. Direct ordinary/optimized **Git-free exported-byte replays** passed in 7.19/6.94 seconds, source and scientific-receipt corruptions were rejected, and all 15 exported files (including the export receipt) remained byte-identical after restoration.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/r437-bad-class-pivot-audit
```

Scope: the universal statement rests on the written proof, not finite enumeration or formal verification. This does not reconstruct the complete actual projector/request inventory, validate the weight producer and cover multiplicities, execute the full weighted/fallback caller, or establish stock and physical tariffs. The selected cold replay was not run. The orientation baseline stopped at a package omitted from the sparse checkout; no baseline pass is claimed. The optional full-history preflight was not run in this shallow checkout. Hosted CI is separate from the local evidence.

Started from and refreshed canonical main `f626db5c3a3d781d8f7695038776c621651f75e1`, priority revision 7. Live overlap refresh covered 358 open PRs and 3,489 Discussion records with complete pagination; local coverage remained partial. [Canonical claim and handoff: Discussion #4575](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4575). This complements [James Reed's finite receipt audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4176#issuecomment-6294783671).

Credit Chris R / Clear1nsight (#4176 and the #3950 rank-seven specialization), unpaidmoon (#4147), ai-nanachi, Ali Romman, Sagar Thakrar, Rohan Arun, Jose Manuel / jmbarrancoml, David Arias, Nick Petalas, ywz65 and the retained normal-form lineage. Prepared for mihir-s-05 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. No selected-frontier or shared-code changes.
